newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Lew re-elected to Coles Myer board.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Lew re-elected to Coles Myer board.

text.p: Coles Myer Ltd director Solomon Lew was re-elected to the board on Tuesday at the annual meeting in Sydney, despite heated opposition from small shareholders.
Proxy votes representing about 400 million shares were voted for Lew's re-election but there were also proxy votes representing 83 million against his reappointment.
A show of hands from the floor was overwhelmingly against Lew's re-election.

Several small shareholders spoke strongly against Lew's re-election, saying his involvement in the so-called Yannon affair and his record of related-policy transactions should disqualify him from the board.
Coles chairman Nobby Clark defended Lew, saying the board was satisfield the Yannon matter was being properly investigated and that Lew should remain on the board.
At several points Clark warned shareholders against making defamatory statements and closed the debate over Lew's reappointment after 1/1-2 hours to jeers from the floor.

Coles, Australia's largest retailer, said in August it had settled a dispute with Lew and Premier Investments Ltd, controlled by Lew, over the 1990 Yannon transaction and would receive A$12 million in compensation.

The Yannon deal was a financial transaction which cost Coles A$18 million and benefited a company associated Lew by a similar sum. The deal was at the centre of a dispute between the company and sacked finance director, Philip Bowman.
The furore over Bowman's sacking eventually led to Lew's demotion from the position of executive chairman. Lew holds about 14 percent of Coles Myer. --Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
